tei:titleStmt.tei:title: נִשְׁמַת אֱמוּנִים
Nishmat Emunim — reshut No5 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Avraham ibn-Ezra

tei:div.tei:head: Nishmat Emunim — reshut No5 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Avraham ibn-Ezra

tei:lg.tei:l: The avid soul shook, they quaked on the day of trouncing,
Bitterly weep year after year, thunderously pronouncing:
Alas! How the city people-full sits isolated. (Lamentations 1:1)
The born ones’ soul shrieked from their burden’s weight,
Bitterly weep the day their foul iniquity was shown straight:
She who was princess of states has become a serf! (Lamentations 1:1)
The rue- and wormwood-sated souls in remote forgotten parts
Bitterly weep, turn away, exiled, with a roar in their hearts:
Weeping, she weeps in the night, her tears on her cheek. (Lamentations 1:2)
The anguished howling souls from the highest Deity’s rage
Bitterly weep, sorrows and woes and dirges none assuage.
Alas, the Master’s anger shadows Zion’s daughter! (Lamentations 2:1)
The rotting souls in the fields every which way,
Bitterly weep that the people-full was widowed that day.
How the faithful town has become a whore! (Isaiah 1:21)
The anxious miserable souls in their captive land
Petition the Deity, them, their children, race, and fruit at hand,
Saying, would that our mouths be as full of song as the sea!

tei:note.tei:p: A line from the prayer, “Nishmat Kol Ḥai”
